caps.text: DECEMBER 1915
On the Russian front, a German army lieutenant...
...worked out the paths of artillery shells
KARL SCHWARZSCHILD
One of Germany's most famous astronomers
Amid the noise of war...
EINSTEIN'S GENERAL RELATIVITY
...he found the first exact solution of its equations
Einstein himself was amazed
But the solution hid a strange boundary
If all of an object's mass is squeezed into a small ball...
...nothing can ever come back out of it
NOT EVEN LIGHT
For the Sun, that ball would be just 6 km wide
For Earth, the size of a marble
Five months later, Schwarzschild was dead
He never knew what his calculation was hiding...
BLACK HOLE
More than 100 years later...
The James Webb Space Telescope found a black hole...
...that may be older than its own galaxy
But the idea was even older than Schwarzschild
The village priest of Thornhill, England...
JOHN MICHELL
...wrote a long letter to his friend Henry Cavendish
Michell also studied earthquakes...
...and his balance was later used to weigh the Earth
Using Newton's gravity, he asked a simple question
What if a star were as dense as the Sun...
...but 500 times wider?
The answer was shocking
Even light would be too slow to escape its gravity
Such a star would be completely invisible
"DARK STARS"
They could be found only by the stars orbiting them
About 200 years later, astronomers did exactly that
Even Einstein didn't believe in Schwarzschild's boundary
He wrote a paper to prove such things could not exist
The same year, in California...
J. ROBERT OPPENHEIMER
...and his student Hartland Snyder found the opposite
When a very massive star runs out of fuel...
...it collapses under its own weight, and never stops
In the end, it is cut off from the universe forever
1 SEPTEMBER 1939
The same day, Germany invaded Poland...
...and World War II began
The world's attention was elsewhere
Oppenheimer went on to lead the atomic bomb project...
...and never returned to the subject
It took 28 more years for them to get a name
JOHN WHEELER
In a lecture, he gave them a short name that stuck...
"BLACK HOLE"
How do you find something not even light escapes?
That was the question facing astronomers
The answer came in X-rays
A small rocket launched from New Mexico...
...caught a bright X-ray source in the constellation Cygnus
CYGNUS X-1
In 1972, astronomers found a giant blue star...
...circling an invisible companion every 5.6 days
The companion was many Suns heavy, yet invisible
Its gravity was pulling gas off the blue star
The falling gas got so hot it glowed in X-rays
Just as Michell wrote, the invisible object gave itself away
STEPHEN HAWKING vs KIP THORNE
Hawking bet that Cygnus X-1 was NOT a black hole
He later called it an "insurance policy"
If black holes didn't exist, at least he'd win the bet
1990: HAWKING CONCEDED
Today: about 7,200 light-years away...
...and 21 times the mass of the Sun
THE FIRST BLACK HOLE EVER IDENTIFIED
Nothing can escape a black hole...
...or so everyone believed
Stephen Hawking found a crack in that rule
He combined Einstein's gravity...
...with the physics of the very small: quantum physics
The result was astonishing
A faint glow leaks out from the edge, the event horizon
HAWKING RADIATION
So black holes don't last forever
They slowly lose energy, and one day evaporate
But very, very slowly
A Sun-mass black hole would take this many years
Hawking radiation has never been observed
No machine today can catch such a faint glow
Perhaps that is why Hawking never won a Nobel Prize
Near a black hole, gravity isn't just strong...
...it's uneven
The side closer to the black hole is pulled much harder
So it gets stretched long and thin, like spaghetti
"SPAGHETTIFICATION"
Seen from far away, a falling object seems to slow...
...as if time itself has stopped
Its light turns red, then dim, then vanishes
About 215 million light-years away...
...a Sun-like star passed too close to a giant black hole
It was ripped into a long stream...
...and about half of its mass was swallowed
VERY LARGE TELESCOPE, CHILE
Telescopes recorded its death for six months
A star's death had never been seen this close
The nearest supermassive black hole...
...sits at the very centre of the Milky Way
26,000 LIGHT-YEARS AWAY
SAGITTARIUS A*
Thick walls of dust lie between it and Earth...
...but infrared light passes straight through
From the 1990s, two teams tracked stars near the centre
REINHARD GENZEL
...using telescopes in Chile
ANDREA GHEZ
...using the Keck telescopes in Hawaii
For three decades, they tracked the stars year after year
One star stood out: S2
It circles something invisible every 16 years
2018: OVER 25 MILLION KM/H
That speed needs about 4 million times the Sun's mass...
...in a space so small, it can only be a black hole
NOBEL PRIZE 2020
Shared with Roger Penrose...
...who showed Einstein's theory makes black holes inevitable
Ghez became only the 4th woman to win the Physics Nobel
14 SEPTEMBER 2015
In America, two giant detectors 3,000 km apart...
...caught the same trembling wave
LIGO
Einstein predicted it 100 years earlier...
...when heavy objects whirl, space and time ripple
GRAVITATIONAL WAVES
But the waves are so weak...
...Einstein doubted they could ever be measured
This wave set out 1.3 billion years ago
Two black holes, 36 and 29 Suns heavy, merged
In the last moment, 3 Suns of mass became pure energy
For a split second, it outshone...
...all the stars in the observable universe combined
At Earth, it stretched LIGO's 4 km arms...
...by 1/1000 of the width of a proton
And still, it was caught
NOBEL PRIZE 2017
Among the winners: Kip Thorne...
...the man who won his bet against Hawking
Until now, only a black hole's effects had been seen...
...never the black hole itself
Photographing something so small, so far away...
...needed a telescope as big as the Earth
So scientists built one
EVENT HORIZON TELESCOPE
From Hawaii to Chile, from Spain to the South Pole...
...radio telescopes watched one spot on the same night
...as if they were one giant telescope
There was too much data to send over the internet
About 1,000 hard drives were flown in by plane
10 APRIL 2019
The world saw a black hole for the first time
At the centre of galaxy M87...
...55 million light-years away...
...a black hole 6.5 billion times the Sun's mass
A ring of glowing gas around deep darkness...
...the black hole's shadow
2022: the Milky Way's own black hole...
...Sagittarius A*, was photographed too
Stephen Hawking proposed a rule
When two black holes merge...
...the new black hole's surface area...
...can never be smaller than the two old ones combined
To test it, a collision had to be measured before and after
For decades, that was impossible
14 JANUARY 2025
LIGO caught the clearest gravitational wave ever
Over a billion light-years away...
...two black holes, each over 30 Suns, merged
The signal was 4 times clearer than in 2015
Clear enough to measure the waves before the collision...
...and the final "ringing" of the new black hole
Total area before: about 240,000 km²
After: about 400,000 km²
54 YEARS LATER, HAWKING WAS RIGHT
But Hawking didn't live to see it
STEPHEN HAWKING 1942–2018
For a long time, black holes had one story
First stars form, then galaxies
Massive stars die and become black holes...
...growing slowly over billions of years
The James Webb Space Telescope shook that story
In the early universe, Webb saw small, red, glowing dots
"LITTLE RED DOTS"
Inside them: black holes far bigger than expected
MAY 2026
A team led by the University of Cambridge...
...weighed the black hole in one of them, QSO1, directly
Its light set out when the universe...
...was only about 700 million years old
50 MILLION TIMES THE SUN'S MASS
And around it, almost no galaxy at all
The black hole alone was 2/3 of all the mass
Its gas was almost pure hydrogen and helium...
...just like right after the Big Bang
The simplest explanation:
THE BLACK HOLE CAME BEFORE ITS GALAXY
Perhaps a giant gas cloud collapsed directly...
...or perhaps...
...IN THE FIRST SECOND OF THE BIG BANG
On a battlefield, Schwarzschild found a strange boundary
Today, humanity has photographed that boundary...
...heard black holes collide...
...and seen them at the dawn of the universe
But the biggest question remains:
WHAT LIES BEYOND THE EVENT HORIZON?
At its very centre, even Einstein's laws break down
The day humanity can look inside that darkness...
...it may finally learn where the universe came from
